critique.evidence: The headline immediately states the claim, the supporting copy explains the rendered-pixels versus retrieval-context seam, and “Reveal hidden injection” gives a recognizable next action. The causal-proof comparison between trusted intent and recorded outcome makes the consequence understandable without narration. However, the tablet navigation visibly overlays the introductory content, and the mobile red-layer evidence is cramped, visually contaminated by underlying ghost text, and difficult to scan. The switch also lacks an explicit on/off state label, weakening action certainty.
critique.fix: Prevent the sticky navigation from covering content at tablet widths; on mobile, remove or strongly suppress the underlying preview behind the red evidence panel and stack its comparison fields with more spacing. Add an explicit switch state such as “Agent vision: On/Off” and make the immediate instruction consistently say “Toggle Agent vision to reveal the hidden retrieval layer.”
